judgment: There is trust, and it is blocked.
If he is wary and holds to the middle: good.
It is good to see the great person.
It is not good to ford the great river.
image: Heaven and water move against each other: Lawsuit.
So the noble one, starting anything,
lines: Do not drag the matter on.
so he goes home and slips away —
and his town's three hundred households
Holding firm: danger. In the end, good.
so he turns back to the charge;
he changes, and rests holding firm.
He may be given a belt of honour,
he is three times stripped of it.

notes.name_en: 訟 is a plea at law; 'Lawsuit', not Wilhelm's 'Conflict'.
notes.judgment: 惕中吉終凶 parsed as middle-course good, end misfortune; 終凶 in its glossary form ('pressed' rejected: no such word).
notes.L6: 鞶帶 a broad belt of rank, given and stripped (褫) three times in a morning.
